questions.question: What approach do all three production computer-use models (Claude, OpenAI CUA, Gemini) share?
options: All use OS accessibility APIs for reliable element targeting
All are vision-based: screenshot in, keyboard/mouse commands out; no OS accessibility APIs
All are restricted to browser-only use cases
All require browser extensions to function
questions.explanation: All three 2026 production computer-use models are purely vision-based: screenshot input, keyboard/mouse output. None use OS accessibility APIs — Claude reads pixels, counts coordinates from reference points for resolution-independent targeting.

questions.question: What is the shared 'untrusted input' contract all three models enforce?
options: All inputs must be validated by an external service
Screenshots, DOM text, tool outputs, PDF content, and anything retrieved is untrusted; only direct user instructions count as permission
Tool outputs are trusted but retrieved web content is not
Everything is treated as untrusted except the system prompt
questions.explanation: All three models treat screenshots, DOM text, tool outputs, PDF content, and any retrieved content as untrusted. OpenAI's CUA docs are explicit: 'only direct instructions from the user count as permission.' Retrieved content can contain prompt-injection payloads.

questions.question: What benchmark numbers did OpenAI CUA report at launch?
options: OSWorld 12%, WebArena 25%
OSWorld 38.1%, WebArena 58.1%, WebVoyager 87%
OSWorld 75%, WebArena 80%
Online-Mind2Web 70%, OSWorld 50%
questions.explanation: OpenAI CUA (Operator, launched January 2025) reported at launch: OSWorld 38.1%, WebArena 58.1%, and WebVoyager 87%.

questions.question: What distinguishes Gemini 2.5 Computer Use's safety approach?
options: It uses a content filter applied to the final output
It has a per-step safety service that assesses each action before execution and rejects unsafe actions
It requires manual human approval for every action
It restricts the model to a pre-approved list of actions
questions.explanation: Gemini 2.5 Computer Use (October 2025) introduced a per-step safety service: a classifier that assesses each action before execution and rejects unsafe ones. This has since become a convergence point for 2026 computer-use safety design.

questions.question: What is the recommended defense for a malicious web page that tries to override agent instructions?
options: Trust the model to ignore injected instructions
Per-step safety classifier, allowlist navigation, human-in-the-loop for sensitive actions, and hard-coded refusals for directives found in retrieved text
Only allow the agent to visit verified websites
Run the agent in a sandboxed environment with no network access
questions.explanation: The 2026 defense doctrine combines: per-step safety classifier, allowlist/blocklist navigation, human-in-the-loop for login/purchase/CAPTCHA, content capture with external storage, and hard-coded refusals for directive-shaped text found in retrieved content.

questions.question: When should you use Claude computer use vs Gemini 2.5 Computer Use?
options: Claude for math; Gemini for writing
Claude for richest desktop support (Ubuntu/Linux automation); Gemini for browser-only tasks with per-step safety built in
Claude for consumer applications; Gemini for enterprise applications
They are interchangeable; pick based on price
questions.explanation: Claude computer use has the richest desktop support and is best for Ubuntu/Linux automation. Gemini 2.5 Computer Use is browser-only (13 actions) but offers lower latency and has per-step safety built in.
